Открыть кабинет помогла Ростовская АЭС: атомщики отремонтировали помещение и подготовили его к установке современного аппарата. За полгода врачи провели уже более 2 500 исследований. «Без поддержки Ростовской АЭС мы не смогли бы установить аппарат и начать работу», — отметила главный врач больницы Елена Стрельцова. 📲 Росэнергоатом в МАХ

articles.title: Multiple milestones for India's nuclear projects
articles.summary: Technical studies have begun onsite for Kakrapar units 5 and 6, two 700 MWe reactors planned for construction in Gujarat; India's Nuclear Fuels Complex is making steam generator tubes to support the fleet mode construction project; and India's small modular reactor project has reached a design milestone.

articles.summary: Slovakia's newest nuclear power unit, Mochovce 4, has been connected and started supplying its first electricity to the grid.

articles.summary: С 14 по 16 октября в Москве проходит главный энергетический форум страны. Представители концерна выступают на сессиях деловой и молодежной программ. articles.title: Viewpoint: Unlocking ASEAN's nuclear potential - a case for regulatory convergence on SMRs
articles.summary: ASEAN's rising electricity demand and decarbonisation goals are driving interest in small modular reactors, but fragmented national regulatory frameworks, limited expertise and financing uncertainty could delay their deployment, write Ming Tan and Stephanie Liaw of engineering, management and development consultancy Mott MacDonald.

articles.title: Sweden’s Studsvik Signs ‘Landmark’ Spent Nuclear Fuel Agreement With Norway
articles.summary: Sweden-based nuclear services company Studsvik has signed what it called a “landmark” agreement to manage Norway’s legacy spent nuclear fuel. The agreement with Norwegian Nuclear Decommissioning (NND), the Norwegian state agency responsible for decommissioning the country’s nuclear facilities, runs until 2055 and has an estimated contractual minimum value of about SEK 875m (€78m, $88m) and a potential total value for Studsvik of SEK 3-4bn.

articles.title: Norwegian used fuel to be stored in Sweden
articles.summary: Norwegian Nuclear Decommissioning has signed an agreement with Swedish nuclear technical services provider Studsvik to manage used nuclear fuel from the former research reactors at Halden and Kjeller.

articles.title: Thorizon, TNO launch MSR materials programme
articles.summary: Molten salt reactor developer Thorizon and Dutch research and technology organisation TNO have launched a materials and corrosion programme to generate the experimental data and predictive models required to qualify materials for molten salt reactors.

MHI delivers replacement steam generators for French reactor
articles.summary: Japan's Mitsubishi Heavy Industries has delivered a further three replacement steam generators to EDF. They are scheduled to be installed in unit 2 of its Cruas nuclear power plant in southeastern France.

articles.title: Milestone for Bruce 4 refurbishment
articles.summary: Installation of the unit's 480 calandria tubes was completed faster than at Bruce 3 as the team carrying out the Major Component Replacement project continues to set new records for CANDU refurbishment.

articles.title: US DOE funding to accelerate molten salt reactor development
articles.summary: The Molten Chloride Reactor Experiment aims to achieve first criticality in 2027, with the US Department of Energy approving cost-shared funding under its Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program.

articles.title: Joint venture formed for six-unit SMR plant in Poland
articles.summary: Poland's SGE and ZE Pak have agreed to establish a joint venture to develop a nuclear power plant in Pątnów which will feature up to six BWRX-300 small modular reactors.

articles.title: Newcleo opens MOX fuel development centre
articles.summary: Innovative nuclear energy company Newcleo has inaugurated its EUR10 million (USD11 million) advanced nuclear fuel engineering, testing and training centre located in Chusclan, in the Gard department in southern France.

articles.title: Maritime Nuclear Startup Bluecore Buys First Uranium For Nuclear Plants On Barges
articles.summary: Bluecore Energy, the Long Beach, US-based floating nuclear power startup, has bought its first supply of uranium hexafluoride (UF6), a low-enriched 4.95% blend of U-235 suitable for a commercial nuclear power installation. The material is being held at a US nuclear fuel facility outside the state of California while Bluecore advances its plans for future fuel fabrication, testing and validation. UF6 is the required form of uranium during the enrichment stage of the nuclear fuel cycle.

articles.title: Westinghouse places initial orders for Polish plant
articles.summary: Westinghouse has placed conditional purchase orders for safety-related modules with four Polish companies, a week after being commissioned to begin ordering long-lead items for the first unit of Poland's planned first nuclear power plant.

articles.title: Namibia takes step towards nuclear power
articles.summary: Namibia's Prime Minister has appointed a Nuclear Commissioner to coordinate preparations for nuclear energy and put in place a structure to provide high-level policy coordination and strategic oversight.

articles.title: Kairos Power automates fuel pebble inspections
articles.summary: A new facility at Kairos Power's Manufacturing Development Campus in Albuquerque, New Mexico, verifies manufacturing specifications and engraves each fuel pebble with a unique code so it can be traced through testing and operation.

articles.title: US maritime nuclear firm Bluecore Energy announces uranium purchase
articles.summary: California-based Bluecore Energy said its purchase of low-enriched uranium from WMC is one of several areas where it has made "significant progress" towards moving its technology from engineering and non-fuelled hardware development toward fuel fabrication, testing, validation and future deployment.

articles.title: Hot testing of Chinese SMR under way
articles.summary: Tests that simulate the temperatures and pressures which the reactor systems will be subjected to during normal operation are reportedly taking place at the ACP100 small modular reactor demonstration project, under construction at the Changjiang site on China's island province of Hainan.

articles.title: IAEA Training Centre Builds Practical Skills for Nuclear Security
articles.summary: The IAEA’s Nuclear Security Training and Demonstration Centre, the world’s first international training centre dedicated to enhancing nuclear security, opened its doors in Seibersdorf, Austria, in October 2023.

articles.title: Bangladesh’s Rooppur-1 Nuclear Plant Achieves First Criticality
articles.summary: Unit 1 at the Rooppur nuclear power station being built by Russia in Bangladesh has achieved criticality with grid connection expected by the end of November. The 1,080-MW VVER V-523 pressurised water reactor unit, construction of which began in 2017, achieved first criticality at 15:34 on 11 October. First criticality is the milestone moment when a nuclear reactor achieves a self-sustaining, controlled chain reaction for the very first time. Rooppur, Bangladesh’s most expensive infrastructure facility, has considerable backing from Russia.

Hot Testing Begins At China’s Linglong-1 Small Modular Reactor
articles.summary: China’s Linglong-1 small modular reactor (SMR) demonstration plant is undergoing hot functional testing, according to unconfirmed reports in local media. The local China News Service reported that the workers at the plant, under construction at the Changjiang nuclear power site in Hainan province in south China, were aiming to meet targets for fuel loading and grid connection before the end of 2026.

articles.title: Constellation To Invest $4.3 Billion In New Nuclear Capacity After Deal With Google
articles.summary: Google and Constellation Energy have announced a long-term collaboration to bring 890 MW of new nuclear capacity onto the grid to meet growing demand and increase grid reliability. The 20-year power purchase agreement will enable investments in new equipment and technology at 11 Constellation-owned nuclear units in Illinois, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey, increasing thermal and electrical efficiency to unlock additional reliable, firm power to serve the grid.

articles.title: Europe Delivers Final Vacuum Vessel Section For €22 Billion Iter Fusion Project
articles.summary: Europe’s final vacuum vessel section for the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (Iter) nuclear fusion project in France has arrived onsite. Fusion for Energy (F4E), the European Union’s organisation for Europe’s contribution to the €22bn ($24.6bn) Iter project, said the component left Westinghouse’s factory in Monfalcone, Italy, and was transported by French industrial conglomerate Daher to the site in Cadarache.
